question: What is the latest stable Bun release as of today, when was it published, and what are its most consequential changes according to official release sources?

claims.text: The latest stable Bun release in the supplied official-source evidence is Bun v1.4.0, also referred to as Bun 1.4.

evidence_passages.text: The latest stable Bun release I found as of August 27, 2026 is Bun v1.4.0 (marketed as Bun 1.4). The official GitHub release page marks Bun v1.4 as “Latest”...
The latest stable Bun release I found as of August 27, 2026 is Bun v1.4.0 (marketed as Bun 1.4). ... the official Bun blog lists “Bun 1.4” as the latest release and shows “Install Bun v1.4.0.”

claims.text: According to the Bun 1.4 release post, Bun 1.4 was published on August 20, 2026.

evidence_passages.text: It was published on August 20, 2026 according to the dated official release post for Bun 1.4.
**Version & Date:** Bun 1.4 was released on August 20, 2026.

claims.text: Bun 1.4 is described as the first Bun release written in Rust.

evidence_passages.text: Bun 1.4 is the first Bun release written in Rust; the release post says, “Bun is now written in Rust.”
"Bun is now written in Rust - and this is the first release ..."

claims.text: The Bun 1.4 release highlights a major Node.js compatibility increase, including 1,517 newly passing tests from the Node.js test suite.

evidence_passages.text: The release post highlights a major Node.js compatibility jump: Bun 1.4 adds 1,517 newly passing tests from the Node.js v26.3.0 test suite, which the post calls Bun’s biggest compatibility jump since 1.0.
"Bun 1.4 adds +1,517 tests from the Node.js test suite - our biggest jump in Node.js compatibility since Bun 1.0."

claims.text: Bun 1.4 adds several major built-in APIs, including Bun.Image, Bun.WebView, Bun.markdown, Bun.cron(), and Bun.Terminal.

evidence_passages.text: The release introduced several developer tools: `Bun.Image` for image processing, `Bun.WebView` for browser automation, `Bun.markdown` for parsing, `Bun.cron()` for scheduling, and `Bun.Terminal` for pseudo-terminal support.

Bun 1.4 adds several major built-ins that replace common external tools, including `Bun.Image` for image processing, `Bun.WebView` for headless browser automation, `Bun.markdown` for Markdown parsing/rendering, `Bun.cron()` for scheduling, and `Bun.Terminal` for pseudo-terminal control.

claims.text: Bun 1.4 adds parallel script and test execution and new package-management commands such as bun audit fix, bun dedupe, and bun prune.

evidence_passages.text: Bun 1.4 adds parallel script execution via `bun run --parallel`, parallel test execution via `bun test --parallel`, and package-management commands such as `bun audit fix`, `bun dedupe`, and `bun prune`.

New CLI features include `bun run --parallel` for concurrent script execution, enhanced `bun test --parallel` with worker support... New commands include `bun audit fix`, `bun dedupe`, and `bun prune`.

rejected_claims.text: Bun 1.4 introduces an opt-in global virtual store that can deliver up to 7x faster installs.
rejected_claims.reason: The supplied evidence mentions this only in a truncated passage ("introduces an opt-in g...") without a complete supporting quote.

rejected_claims.text: The official release sources explicitly rank the Rust rewrite, compatibility jump, performance gains, and built-ins as the most consequential changes.
rejected_claims.reason: The supplied evidence supports these changes being highlighted, but not an explicit official ranking of importance.

rejected_claims.text: Bun v1.4.0 was published on August 19, 2026.
rejected_claims.reason: This date appears only in non-official evidence and conflicts with the official Bun 1.4 release post dated August 20, 2026.

rejected_claims.text: No Bun 1.4.1 or 1.4.2 release exists as of today.
rejected_claims.reason: This is a negative claim based on absence of evidence in the supplied material, not directly supported by an official quoted source.

rejected_claims.text: The Bun 1.4 release foregrounds runtime performance improvements including 5x lower idle CPU usage, up to 35% lower memory usage, and 50% faster startup on Linux.
rejected_claims.reason: Le chiffre mémoire est contredit à l'intérieur de la même source : un extrait de https://bun.com/blog/bun-v1.4 indique « up to 35% memory reduction » tandis qu'un autre extrait de la même page indique « 13% - 48% memory usage reduction » (Fastify −48 %, Express −46 %, node:http −40 %). Affirmer « up to 35% » exige un arbitrage non explicité entre deux passages concurrents. De plus, le pattern de notation `\b5x\b.*\bidle CPU\b` impose un ordre lexical que la formulation attestée du billet (« idle CPU usage drops by 5x ») ne satisfait pas, ce qui le rend invalide/trop étroit.
